sentences.text: This Civil Revision Petition is filed invoking the provisions of Article 227 of the Constitution of India, aggrieved by the order dated 08.10.2024 passed by the I Additional District and Sessions Judge, Kamareddy in I.A.No.286 of 2024 in O.P.No.84 of 2023, where-under the application filed by the petitioner seeking permission to file additional counter affidavit was dismissed.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Kamareddy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard Smt. T. Padmaja, learned counsel representing Mr. Harinath Reddy Soma, learned counsel for revision petitioner.
In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 has not chosen to enter appearance.

3. Brief facts of the case:
Respondent No.1 filed O.P.No.84 of 2023 on the file of I Additional District and Sessions Judge, Kamareddy claiming compensation to an Rs.4,00,000/- against the petitioner-Insurance Company and respondent No.2 on the ground that he sustained injuries in the accident which was occurred on 06.03.2023, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of respondent No.2 vehicle lorry bearing No.TS-01-UA-4373.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Kamareddy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the said O.P., petitioner filed counter denying the averments made by respondent No.1.

Petitioner filed application I.A.No.286 of 2024 seeking permission to file additional counter affidavit, the said application was dismissed by the trial Court on the ground that the petitioner without assailing the valid reasons filed the application to protract the litigants one way or other.
Thus, the petitioner filed revision petition.

4. Learned counsel for petitioner submitted that the respondent No.1 filed O.P.No.84 of 2023 by producing fake policy though the said policy is not existing, filed O.P. basing upon Ex.A5 policy document.
Basing on the said document, respondent No.1 is not entitled to seek any compensation against the petitioner-Insurance Company.

To establish the said fact, the petitioner wants to file additional counter affidavit and the petitioner Company is not withdrawing any admission made in the counter affidavit which already filed and by virtue of the same, no prejudice is going to be caused to the respondent No.1.
Learned counsel further submits that the petitioner is not going to adduce any further evidence in the matter.
5. This Court considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for petitioner and perused the material available on record.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the respondent No.1 filed O.P.No.84 of 2023 in the month of July, 2023 claiming compensation invoking the provision of Motor Vehicles Act against the petitioner as well as respondent No.1 claiming an amount of Rs.3,00,000/-.
In the said O.P., petitioner filed counter affidavit/written statement in the month of October, 2023.

When the matter reached for arguments,
petitioner filed I.A.No.286 of 2024 and also filed another I.A.No.287 of 2024 seeking permission to file additional counter affidavit and also to demark the Ex.A5 document, the Court below dismissed the above two applications on 08.10.2024.
Aggrieved by the same, petitioner filed two revision petitions i.e., C.R.P.Nos.3589 of 2024 and 3598 of 2024.

7. In this revision petition, the petitioner seeks permission to file any counter affidavit only for the purpose the Ex.A5 document placed by respondent No.1 is not in existence and basing on the said document, respondent No.1 is not entitled to claim any compensation.

Learned counsel submitted that the petitioner is not going to adduce any evidence, the petitioner has already filed additional counter along with I.A.No.286 of 2024.
8.

In view of the averments made in the application in I.A.No.286 of 2024 as well as the submissions made by learned counsel for petitioner, this Court is inclined to grant permission to the petitioner to file additional counter only to the extent to elaborate the stand taken in the earlier counter in respect of existence of Ex.A5.
9.

For the foregoing reasons, the impugned order passed by the trial Court, dated 08.10.2024 is set aside and the petitioner is permitted to file additional counter as mentioned supra within a period of one week from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
10. Accordingly, the civil revision petition is disposed of.
No order as to costs.

Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
______________________________ JUSTICE J.SREENIVAS RAO 10.01.2025

Note:
Issue C.C. in three (3) days.
